text: Teresa is having her gallbladder out on Thursday morning. She sounded quite nervous about the anaesthetic. I should text her on Wednesday evening to wish her luck.
Mateo has gone vegan since the summer. No honey either, apparently he's strict about it.
Lunch with Meera and Anan. Meera is coeliac, so the Italian place is out. Anan only drinks oat flat whites and will tell you about it at length.

Tamar's dad had a fall at the weekend and is in hospital until at least Monday. She's driving up tomorrow morning. He's eighty-four and already complaining about the hospital food, which she says is a good sign. Her brother Rhys can't get there until Friday, so she's on her own for a few days. Need to ring her on Tuesday to see how he's doing.
Dong mentioned he's allergic to shellfish, properly allergic, carries an EpiPen. Worth remembering before the work dinner.
Theo and Jada are coming round for dinner on Saturday at 7. Jada doesn't eat pork. I'm doing the lamb tagine.
Rana's knee operation went well yesterday. She's on crutches for six weeks and already bored out of her mind. Must drop round some books sometime next week.
Zainab says the hospital have finally given her a date for the MRI: the 14th at twenty past eight in the morning.
Keisha's off sugar for the whole of November. Don't bring her the brownies.
Called Leon. His mum's hip replacement has been pushed back again, now looking like early March. He's frustrated with the waiting list but trying to stay patient.
Nora loves really peaty whisky, Laphroaig especially. Christmas present sorted, probably.
Pick up the prescription from Boots before Friday at 5. Also cancel the dentist, I can't make the Wednesday slot.
Jun's cat Biscuit had a tooth out at the vet this morning. He's fine, just sulking. Jun was more stressed than Biscuit was.
Omar is fasting until the end of the month, so no coffee meet-ups during the day. Suggested dinner instead, sometime the week after next.

Mabel's 80th birthday lunch is on Sunday the 9th at half twelve. Her daughter Saskia is organising it and asked me to bring a pudding. Mabel can't have nuts, so no frangipane. Thinking a lemon posset, or the sticky toffee pudding she raved about last year. Saskia also hinted that Mabel would love a framed photo of the old house, so maybe chip in with the cousins for that.

Olga starts chemo next Tuesday. She was very matter of fact about it on the phone but I could tell she's scared. Remind me to send her a card this week and to call her on the Wednesday after the first session.
Cem has started doing intermittent fasting, eats only between twelve and eight. Explains why he never comes to breakfast.
Nadia and her husband are going to Lisbon at the end of the month for their anniversary. She wants restaurant tips. I should send her the list from our trip.
Jaya had her wisdom teeth out on Monday. Face like a hamster, living on soup and ice cream. Text her tomorrow afternoon to see how she's healing.
Simone hates coriander. Genuinely hates it, says it tastes like soap.

Planning the barbecue with Noor this afternoon. Yosef keeps kosher, so the barbecue on the 21st needs separate stuff for him. I'm getting him his own grill tray. Noor said she'll handle the drinks, and she only drinks alcohol-free beer these days anyway.
Saskia mentioned she'd love a decent coffee grinder. She keeps borrowing her sister's. Filing that away for her birthday in January.
Layla's surgery has been cancelled. The consultant wants to try physio first for three months, so she's relieved more than anything. Need to check how the first physio session goes next Thursday.
Sunil is cooking for us at his new flat sometime over the summer. He's very into Keralan food at the moment and has been perfecting his fish curry.
Lachlan sounded rough on the phone. He's had a chest infection for two weeks and finally sees the GP tomorrow at 10:40. I said I'd drop off soup this evening.
Rhys is lactose intolerant, which I completely forgot when I made the cheese board. Felt terrible. Get some proper dairy-free cheese for next time.
Quick catch up with Leah. She's moving to Bristol at the start of December and is already worrying about finding a GP.
Caitlin's mum has her cataract surgery on the 3rd at 2pm. Caitlin is taking her and staying the night. I should message Caitlin that evening to see how it went.
Meera Kumar from work, the one who brings in the lime pickle, is retiring at the end of March. Her leaving lunch will probably be the last Friday of the month.
Theodore, Theo to everyone, has joined a running club and has given up beer until after his half marathon in April. He's surprisingly happy about it.
Need to book my flu jab. Sometime next week, ideally a morning.
Mateo's sister Olga had her baby on Saturday night, a little girl. Mateo is a very proud uncle already. Must send something for the baby, maybe that knitted blanket from the market.
Teresa's recovering well. She's back home since Friday and eating normally again, mostly toast and tea. Her son Leon is staying with her until the weekend.
Anan's off caffeine for his blood pressure. He's switched to rooibos and is not thrilled.
Spoke to Noor about her dad. He's in for a stent tomorrow morning at 7 and should be home by Thursday. She's holding it together but only just. I'll ring her tomorrow night.
Dong and Jun are hosting a dumpling night on the 18th at 6:30. I'm bringing beer. Jun asked me to check whether Keisha's coming because she's veggie and they'll do a separate batch.
Zainab's scan results came back clear. Huge relief all round. Should send her flowers this week.
Jada said she can't stand mushrooms in any form. Also she's trying to cut down on wine during the week.

Rana's brother Cem is in hospital after a cycling accident on Sunday morning. Broken collarbone and a few stitches, nothing worse thankfully. She's going up to see him on Wednesday. I want to send him something to keep him busy, maybe a puzzle book, and I should ask Rana sometime next week how his recovery's going.
Nora has her follow-up with the cardiologist on Monday the 2nd at 11. She's been a bit anxious since the last one.
Bought the oat milk, still need bread. Bins go out Tuesday night.
Keisha mentioned her dog Pepper is booked in to be spayed on Friday. She's dreading it more than the dog will.

Leon's grandmother passed away last week. The funeral is on the 27th at 1pm. I'm going with Mabel, and we'll drive up together that morning. She was very close to him too. Leon said his grandmother made the best baklava in the family, and his aunt is making a batch for the wake. Remember to send Leon a message the morning of the funeral.
Omar loves Turkish delight, the rose kind specifically. Good gift idea for when he finishes his course.

Simone and Yosef have called off the trip to Japan in November because of his back. He's seeing a specialist at the end of the month instead. Simone is gutted, they'd been planning it for two years, but she says his health comes first. She's thinking they might rebook for over the summer instead. Must check in with Simone after that appointment.

Jaya's daughter has her tonsils out on Tuesday at 9am. Jaya is a nervous wreck about it, even though the surgeon told her it's routine and they'll be home by teatime. Her husband can only get the morning off. I should drop round a lasagne on Wednesday so she doesn't have to cook.
Sunil told me he's gone gluten free on his doctor's advice. Not coeliac, they think, but the tests are pending in the new year.

Had coffee with Caitlin. She says Rhys is the fussiest eater she knows, will only eat pasta with butter and cheese. Rhys also hates anything spicy and picks the onions out of everything. They're coming to the barbecue on the 21st, probably arriving late afternoon, so I'll plan around it and do a plain pasta salad on the side.
Lachlan's GP thinks it's just a lingering virus, but he's been signed off work until Friday.
Mrs Novak next door has asked me to water her plants while she's in hospital, Tuesday until roughly the following Monday. Key is under the blue pot.
Layla said her mum Teresa is coming over from Madrid for Christmas and she's a strict vegetarian. Layla is panicking about the menu already.
Meera's surgery went fine yesterday afternoon. She's in for one more night. Video call her tomorrow at lunchtime and see if she needs anything brought in.
Theo prefers red wine, Jada prefers white, and neither of them will touch rosé.
Tamar and her partner Nadia are both doing Dry January together. Nadia says it's mainly to support Tamar, who's trying to sleep better.
Uncle Sunil is having his pacemaker fitted sometime early next month. Mum wants me to visit him the weekend after and bring the photos from the wedding.
Need to send Anan the recipe for the lentil soup before Saturday. He asked twice.

Zainab Olsen from the choir is going in for a hysterectomy on the 19th. Her husband is taking a fortnight off to look after her. She's not nervous, she says, just keen to get it done. She can't have anything with nuts, so when I make the get well basket I'll avoid the granola and stick to fruit, tea, and that lemon shortbread she likes. Aim to drop it round the weekend after she's home.
Cem's back at work after the hospital stay, but still on a soft food diet for another two weeks.
Jun is trying to get into natural wine and keeps sending me photos of labels. Must find that bar in Peckham for us to try sometime in early spring.

Long chat with Saskia tonight. Her partner Lachlan finally had his hernia op on Monday and it was more complicated than expected, so he was kept in until Thursday afternoon. He's home now but in a lot of pain and grumpy about not being able to lift anything. She's exhausted and sounded like she's struggling a bit. Plan: take her out for brunch on Sunday morning, and ask Lachlan whether he wants me to walk their dog Mochi on weekday evenings for the next couple of weeks.
